extracted.intended_audience: federal agency standards managers, Standards Executives, program managers responsible for OMB Circular A-119 reporting and standards policy
extracted.subtask_short: OMB A-119 reporting on standards use
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting requirements for federal agencies on participation in, use of, substitution for, and evaluation of voluntary consensus standards under OMB Circular A-119 and P.L. 104-113. Includes example rationales, procedures, and agency practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting: number of voluntary consensus standards bodies and participating employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of voluntary consensus standards bodies in which there is Agency participation and the number of employees participating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should report counts and may list organizations and subgroups (examples provided: ANSI, ASTM, ISO, IEC, NFPA, etc.). Note that simple employee counts may not capture multiple committee memberships; improved tracking formats are recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting: number of voluntary consensus standards used since Oct 1, 1997
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of voluntary consensus standards the Agency has used since October 1, 1997, based on procedures in sections 11 and 12 of the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report use in regulations (e.g., incorporation by reference), procurement, and proposed rules. Examples: EPA reported 6 final regulations incorporating >90 standards in 1998 and 10 proposed regulations referencing 67 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting: identification of VCS substituted for government-unique standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify voluntary consensus standards that have been substituted for government-unique standards as a result of an Agency review under the Circular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples and describe review processes (e.g., EPA Emission Measurement Center search of NSSN). Note positive examples (e.g., adoption of ANSI/ASQC E4 as the technical basis for Agency-wide quality system) and list substituted standard identifiers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting: evaluation of Circular A-119 effectiveness and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation of the effectiveness of Circular A-119 policy and any recommendations for changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide agency assessment (EPA: endorsed revised Circular, no changes recommended at this time). Discuss operational effects, minor issues, and suggested improvements if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting: instances using government-unique standards instead of VCS (with rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of all instances when the agency used government-unique standards in lieu of voluntary consensus standards; for each instance include the agency rationale and the specific government-unique standard used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List Federal Register citations and explain technical or enforcement rationales (examples: EPA cited ASTM D-3960 as impractical due to unspecified units and enforcement difficulty; EPA Method 1650 used because VCS lacked required QA/QC criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards Executive role and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation and duties of the Agency Standards Executive who represents the agency on standards policy matters and implements Circular requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include providing guidance to Commissioners/agency leadership, monitoring agency standards-setting activities, producing required OMB Circular A-119 reports, developing a five-year standards review cycle, and coordinating with Office of General Counsel and program offices. (FCC example lists specific duties a–d.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for rejecting a voluntary consensus standard in favor of a government-unique standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive reasons an agency may determine a particular VCS is impractical or inadequate and therefore retain/develop a government-unique standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include: VCS contains requirements beyond regulatory needs (unnecessary elements); VCS omits essential specifics (e.g., unspecified units) risking inconsistent application and enforcement; VCS lacks standardized QA/QC criteria required for data verification/validation (EPA water programs example); sample preparation and QC procedures not sufficiently similar, risking underreporting. Examples with FR citations are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible uses of voluntary standards by agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: How agencies may use voluntary consensus standards: to satisfy industry/user requirements where mandatory standards are unnecessary; to correct problems that might otherwise require regulation; or as the basis for mandatory requirements by incorporation by reference or inclusion of normative content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FCC examples: using industry standards for network protocols, measurement procedures, and avoiding additional regulation when industry standards suffice. Agencies may incorporate VCS by reference into rules or use their normative portions directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards adoption process and approval chain (example: NASA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural steps and governance for adopting voluntary consensus standards within an agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASA example: adoptions based on staff recommendations, concurrence of an Engineering Standards Steering Council, and formal approval by the Engineering Management Council (EMC) and the NASA Standards Executive. Agencies may use a 'categorical' standards management system for reporting adoptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking and management of employee participation in standards activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms for accurately tracking agency participation in standards bodies and committee work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize multiple memberships per employee; develop a more accurate tracking format (models available from NIST and DOE). Ensure right personnel are on appropriate committees, reassign or drop committee work as needed, and develop participation guides and training to maximize benefit from committee involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics guidance for federal employee participation in standards development
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency ethics guidance reconciling conflict-of-interest rules with the NTTAA directive that Federal employees participate in voluntary standards development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New EPA guidance (Sept 1998) reconciles criminal code provisions on financial conflicts with NTTAA, relying on OLC and OGE memoranda; provides pathways allowing employee membership, service on boards, and committee chairs subject to ethics rules. A copy of the guidance is attached (per EPA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for accepting third-party conformity assessments in voluntary programs
rubrics_metrics.description: How agencies determine acceptability of third-party certification/conformity assessment results for voluntary agency programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: StarTrack (EPA Region I) accepts ISO 14001 conformity assessments performed by ANSI-RAB accredited registrars as meeting program EMS implementation and third-party certification requirements. Agencies should evaluate the extent to which such assessments meet program-specific compliance certification requirements before acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits and operational drivers for adopting consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors motivating agency adoption/use of consensus standards: cost-savings, operational efficiency, interoperability, portability, scalability, availability of training/documentation/upgrades, and encouraging competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FEMA cites interoperability, portability and scalability as priorities for IT architecture; availability of training/documentation and modest-cost upgrades are important for adoption; EPA cites benefits in regulatory uniformity and resolving long-standing practical problems (e.g., QA for opacity monitors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting method choices: procurement-transaction tracking vs categorical reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Options for how agencies report use of standards: tracking individual procurement transactions that use standards or using a categorical/standards-management-system approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASA uses a categorical approach via its Technical Standards Management System (listing preferred standards, participants, and links). Agencies should choose/report a method consistent with their usage patterns and systems.
